reports.title: The Government Wants to Test AI Before You Get It
reports.subtitle: Microsoft, Google, and xAI will hand unreleased models to federal scientists. The real story is what triggered it: Anthropic's Mythos.

reports.title: SCOTUS Ended the Nationwide Injunction. Kavanaugh Told You Why.
reports.subtitle: The Court didn't strip power from the judiciary. It moved that power upstairs, to itself.

reports.title: Trump Launched Project Freedom. Then Stopped It After One Day.
reports.subtitle: The Hormuz pause is not a concession to Iran. It is a test of whether Pakistan can deliver a deal before Iran's economy forces one.

reports.title: The Bond Market Thinks Warsh Will Hike Before He Cuts
reports.subtitle: Trump wants cheaper money. His Fed pick may deliver the opposite. And neither man is fully wrong.

reports.title: Australia's Teen Social Media Ban Is Five Months Old. 61% of Affected Kids Still Have Accounts.
reports.subtitle: Meta's AI enforcement tools are a compliance performance, not a solution. The gap between the ban's ambition and its mechanics is now evidence.

reports.title: Nvidia Has Zero Percent of China's AI Market. Its CEO Says That Was Always the Point.
reports.subtitle: Jensen Huang admits export controls handed China's AI chip market to Huawei. He is arguing this proves the policy should be reversed. He has a conflict of interest the size of a data center.

reports.title: The Senate Banned Prediction Markets in Hours. It Has Never Managed to Ban Stock Trading.
reports.subtitle: Senators passed a unanimous rule banning themselves from Polymarket and Kalshi in a single day. The same body has failed for years to pass stock trading restrictions. The asymmetry is not an accident.

reports.title: The EU Made a Deal with Trump. Trump Is Now Threatening to Break It Over Greenland.
reports.subtitle: Brussels struck a July 2025 agreement setting tariffs at 15%. Trump threatened 25% on cars last week. The EU is asking Washington to honor the deal it signed nine months ago. Washington is not answering.

reports.title: UAW Is Threatening to Strike the Plant That Builds Stellantis' Most Profitable Truck.
reports.subtitle: The fight is about who fixes the machines, not who builds the cars. Skilled trades outsourcing is the knife Stellantis is using to cut labor costs, and the UAW is finally picking it up.

reports.title: Supermicro's Co-Founder Was Indicted for Smuggling $2.5 Billion in AI Chips to China. The Stock Jumped 18%.
reports.subtitle: The market decided the indictment was contained and the guidance was real. One of those bets is probably right.

reports.title: Germany Is Gutting the EU AI Act. Siemens and Bosch Are Watching.
reports.subtitle: Berlin secured an industrial machinery exemption that rewrites the law's core premise: that AI rules should apply to all sectors equally.

reports.title: The 5th Circuit Ended Telehealth Abortion. SCOTUS Has One Week to Decide if It Agrees.
reports.subtitle: Louisiana got a unanimous appeals court to revive an in-person requirement the FDA dropped years ago. The Supreme Court's one-week stay runs out May 11.

reports.title: Both Sides Declared Ceasefires. Russia Launched 100 Drones Anyway.
reports.subtitle: The Victory Day truces were not failed negotiations. They were proof of concept for a tactic: announce peace to prevent counterstrikes, then keep attacking.

reports.title: SCOTUS Gutted the Voting Rights Act. Then It Rushed the Ruling Into Effect.
reports.subtitle: The Court didn't just strike down Louisiana's map. It expedited the ruling so Louisiana can draw a new one in time for 2026 midterms, while Jackson and Alito traded public insults about what that means.

reports.title: Liberation Day Is One Year Old. Moody's Says It Did 'Significant Damage.' Courts Are About to Force Refunds.
reports.subtitle: Job growth stalled. Inflation stayed above target. The IEEPA tariffs were ruled illegal. Polymarket gives 81.5% odds the courts force refunds by June. The White House calls it a success.

reports.title: The Government Will Test Your AI Before You Get It. The Companies Volunteered.
reports.subtitle: NIST signed testing agreements with Google, Microsoft, and xAI. The trigger was Anthropic's Mythos. The structure rewards the compliant and punishes no one.

reports.title: One Year After Operation Sindoor, Both India and Pakistan Are Preparing for the Next War
reports.subtitle: The ceasefire is holding. The lessons both sides drew from the last conflict are not about how to prevent the next one. They are about how to win it.

reports.title: $175 Billion in Tariff Refunds Are Starting to Flow. The Fight Over Who Gets Them Is Just Beginning.
reports.subtitle: Large multinationals have customs teams ready. Small importers are still figuring out the portal. The money goes to whoever filed correctly, not to whoever paid the most.

reports.title: SCOTUS Will Strike Down Trump's Birthright Citizenship Order. The Real Question Is What It Lets Happen First.
reports.subtitle: Polymarket gives 87% odds the Court kills the executive order. But SCOTUS already ruled states can enforce it partially. A ruling that arrives in June matters less than what happens between now and June.

reports.title: 900 Health Facilities Are At Risk of Closing. States Are Trying to Fill a Hole They Cannot Fill.
reports.subtitle: The One Big Beautiful Bill cut $911 billion from Medicaid over ten years. The rural health fund it created to compensate is $50 billion over five years. The math does not balance.

reports.title: Trump Officially Moved Terrorism's Address from the Middle East to Mexico City.
reports.subtitle: The new counterterrorism strategy makes Western Hemisphere cartels the top priority and jihadists second. That is not rhetoric. It is a reallocation of the entire U.S. counterterrorism apparatus.
